purpose: Radar of HIGH/MEDIUM findings still actionable. Epistemic statuses preserved; nothing here certifies scientific truth. The Chief CTO must route any new claim to a lane/team for validation before use.

findings.summary: First repo-hygiene execution permanently deleted the raw Actions logs of 102 runs. For 4 of the 5 deleted Critical CTO Council runs no run-id-attributable durable artifact exists anywhere in Git; whether those reviews contained unique advisory prescriptions is unknowable post-deletion (loss_assessment=UNKNOWN). The other 98 deletions are assessed NONE_MATERIAL (orchestration-only, or fully recovered).
actionable_next: Decide whether any pre-CTO-4 council pass needs reconstruction from any surviving side channel (none currently known); if not, close the UNKNOWNs as accepted residual risk.
Do not treat reconstructed summaries of the four UNKNOWN council runs as evidence; none exists.

findings.summary: Recoverability gap is structural, not accidental: exactly one deleted run (council run 32876814203) had persisted its output before pruning (origin/lab/cto@6b1f030); all other deleted runs left nothing attributable. Council/supervisor/workdog workflows emit no durable receipt tying their run id to their effects.
actionable_next: Require every autonomous workflow (cto-council, *-supervisor, watchdogs, hygiene) to commit a run-id-attributed receipt before completion, so future pruning cannot orphan outputs.
Gate future hygiene passes on evidence/run-memory safe_to_prune flags instead of recency heuristics only.

findings.summary: The hygiene script version that executed the 102 deletions (commit 3e5ea6d) had no distillation requirement; maintainers hardened it after the fact (1afb229 'require durable run distillation before pruning', a09d036 'restore durable-reference protection'). Until the hardened version has executed successfully, assume un-distilled claim-bearing logs could still be pruned by a stale workflow version.
actionable_next: Verify the next hygiene dispatch runs the hardened script and that run 32880942022 itself stays protected (its log is the sole deletion manifest; safe_to_prune=false).

findings.summary: Orchestration noise dominates Actions economics: 102 supervisor/watchdog/council runs were created in ~18.2h (~5.6/h; Ox Watchdog alone = 39) versus 54 retained substantive runs. Each hygiene pass costs ~43s of sequential DELETE API calls per 100 deletions.
actionable_next: Evaluate consolidating watchdog/supervisor cadence or event-triggering them instead of fixed heartbeats; measure runner minutes saved against recovery-latency risk before changing anything.

findings.summary: Permission auto-rejection is a single point of failure for lane agent sessions: in Graph run 32782331702 one out-of-workspace access ('cd /home/runner/work/Spider' -> external_directory auto-reject) aborted the ENTIRE team session after ~7m of context loading, producing a zero-commit production snapshot that the workflow then pushed and audited anyway (~9m audit spent detecting it). The same empty-snapshot class recurred in Intel's repair round 2 (per accepted INTEL_LEDGER history), so it is cross-lane and recurring, not a one-off.
actionable_next: Harden the agent runtime so a single permission denial degrades gracefully (skip tool call) instead of terminating the session; pre-authorize known-safe parent paths in the lane workflows.
Add a zero-diff guard after each team phase: if the team branch equals its base, return to coder immediately instead of consuming an independent-audit job.

Confirm root cause by reproducing the abort signature before treating the fix as verified; the log-only evidence lives only in /tmp/spider_run_evidence/32782331702/logs.txt and this run's Actions log.

findings.summary: WP-006 instrument post-mortem (falsified result already accepted; this is forward-looking only): a site hard-timeout silently skipped the per-site BP-manifest dump, so the merged manifest omitted openlibrary; every manifest-fed check (verifier C2 coverage 868/910 undisclosed, D5 calibration) then 'passed' with reduced coverage, and the team report misstated its own FN control (62/62 vs raw-row truth 62/74; finalized 67/74 after repairs). Additionally one frozen ordinal-0 anchor slot rule systematically selected non-actionable skip-links on two site skins (171 action_failed exclusions; 24 BPs zeroed). No hard validity gate caught any of this — only adversarial per-row recomputation did.
durable_refs: git:origin/lab/physics commits a00dc6a..0be8d8a (repair chain, corrected arithmetic, 5-gate acceptance)
actionable_next: If any future interventional Web collection is chartered: require per-site artifact-completion assertions at collection end, audited coverage denominators, and slot-selection rules robust to accessibility scaffolding (no frozen ordinal anchors); do NOT reopen WP-006 itself (frozen stop rule stands).

findings.summary: Report-vs-data drift recurred in all three lanes within one day while aggregates stayed numerically correct: Physics WP-006 FN-control misstatement (62/62 claimed), Intel SGDR wins attributed to the wrong site cluster in prose (login/pager claimed; actually all the-internet dynamic-loading clusters), Graph cycle-3 E2 residual used non-reproducible denominators. Independent auditors caught all three via from-scratch recomputation against committed raw rows; none was measurement fraud, but self-reported decompositions are unreliable inputs for Director decisions (the WP-006 misstatement fed a lane-termination decision).
actionable_next: Consider requiring reports to generate decomposition claims mechanically from the committed raw rows (script-generated tables with row-linked provenance) so prose cannot diverge from data; strengthen auditor checklists to always recompute per-cell decompositions, not just headline aggregates.

findings.summary: The lane workflows' 'Enforce audit-only writes' gate false-positives on workflow-pre-staged control-plane files and kills COMPLETED audits: it tests `git status --porcelain` against allowed output dirs, but an earlier workflow step pre-stages role/directive sync files into the index, which get attributed to the auditor. Physics run 32793165981: auditor had already written gate=PASS/safe_to_integrate=true when the gate exited 1 → run conclusion=failure, Lane Director skipped. Graph run 32793580374: REVISE delivered, then the deterministic failure repeated across EIGHT re-run attempts (~18m audit each, ~13h wall-clock span), eight audit-attempt branches pushed, Director never ran. The gate also masks real violations by mixing plumbing noise into the same signal.
actionable_next: Fix both loop workflows: scope the write check to changes made during the audit session (e.g. diff working tree vs the commit HEAD at session start) or unstage control-plane sync before the audit agent runs.
Add retry-loop damping: if an audit attempt fails with the identical violation set twice, fail loudly instead of re-running the full audit.
After fixing, verify by replaying one physics and one graph cycle end-to-end (Director job must execute).

findings.summary: A second, EARLIER pruning event predates the tombstone process: one-shot cleanup run 32790538553 deleted 21 completed runs at 2026-08-24T23:42Z, including TWO claim-bearing SPIDER Graph Lane runs (32776369696 success, 32689296167 failure) whose raw logs are gone. Claim-level loss is NONE_MATERIAL (cycle/* team+audit branches survive; director-integrated into lab/graph via f42c14d/c1dd8e3), but log-only operational diagnostics are irrecoverable and the deletion manifest itself survives ONLY in that run's raw log. Root cause is a keep-rule flaw: 'keep latest completed run per current workflow name' deletes older runs of ACTIVE workflows too. This event is disjoint from the 102-run hygiene incident (CF-01); together they are the complete known pruning history.
durable_refs: git:origin/lab/graph@f42c14d / c1dd8e3 (durable integrations of the two deleted Graph Lane runs)
actionable_next: Protect runs non-recursively by distillation state, not recency: never prune a completed run that owns cycle/* branches or lacks a safe_to_prune=true record, regardless of workflow-name recency.
Optionally authorize a small recovery pass promoting ids 32776369696/32689296167 from runs/32790538553.json to deleted/<id>.json tombstones; the other 19 deletions are orchestration-only.
Keep run 32790538553's raw log protected until its manifest is duplicated into durable memory (its record currently carries it).

findings.summary: Silent repair-delivery loss mechanism identified (Intel SGDR repair round 2): the reproducer committed its complete documentary fix set on DETACHED HEAD inside a private lineage workspace (/tmp/spider_intel_repro_r2, commit 0a1b3ef), while the workflow's persist step force-pushed a DIFFERENT mounted workspace still sitting at the base commit — publishing a branch byte-identical to lab/intel base with every step exiting success. ~40m of work vanished; only the independent auditor's empty-snapshot identity check (run_tip == base == 0a55649, tree 00ce8e32) plus hidden-output/displaced-work elimination prevented a wrong verdict, and its RF-E ('verify delivery') defines the fix. This is mechanism-distinct from the permission-abort empty snapshot of Graph #5 (CF-05).
actionable_next: Add post-persist assertions to all lane loops: pushed tip != base commit AND required deliverable paths exist in the pushed tree; treat violation as immediate job failure before any downstream job runs.
Mount ONE canonical workspace per agent phase (or persist from the workspace the agent was last seen committing in) so lineage commits cannot diverge from the published ref.
Adopt the auditor's escalation rule: two consecutive empty/unverifiable deliveries ⇒ BLOCKED on infrastructure grounds.

findings.summary: Control-plane contradiction killed the Runtime lane's first real cycle post-completion (run 32887030457): docs/CTO_TO_RUNTIME.md FIRST COMMIT items 1–2 order the team to build directives/COST_EVENT.md + schemas/spider.{cost_event,capsule,plan}.v0.schema.json ('next lane commit must produce the COST_EVENT pack or a schema/validator/benchmark artifact'), but 'Enforce Runtime scope' in runtime-loop.yml line 140 — unchanged since workflow creation at 7669dcd — allows neither path. The team followed the charter; after ~64 minutes of green work (prereg-frozen pilot, VERDICT PASS 6/6 gates, 58/58 tests) the gate flagged exactly BAD='directives/COST_EVENT.md'+'schemas/' and failed the run, skipping Auditor and Director; lab/runtime untouched. Mechanism is DISTINCT from CF-2026-08-25-08 (porcelain false positive on pre-staged files): here the violation is real but mandated by another control-plane document. The stale allowlist is still live at main HEAD, so every future scheduled Runtime run fails identically until fixed. Evidence survived: cycle/runtime/32887030457/team@c2f0ba8e was pushed despite the gate.
durable_refs: git:origin/lab/cto:docs/CTO_TO_RUNTIME.md (charter items ordering the flagged paths)
actionable_next: One-line fix: extend the runtime-loop.yml scope allowlist with directives/COST_EVENT\.md$ and schemas/ (or relocate shared schemas into an allowed namespace agreed by CTO + Product as D8 co-owner), then audit c2f0ba8e instead of re-running the team from scratch.
Sweep ALL lane loop workflows for the same charter-vs-gate drift class before their next scheduled dispatch (compare each gate regex against the current CTO_TO_* charters).
Decide policy: when a CTO charter orders cross-cutting artifacts outside a lane's historical write scope, the charter dispatch must update the gate in the same change.

durable_refs: git:origin/cycle/runtime/32887030457/team@c2f0ba8e30effa1f5afb6e957adb3efd9c2a8558 (PREREG_R0_CYCLE1.json, pilot VERDICT/raw_rows/cost_events, RUNTIME_LEDGER.md findings C1–C5, NEXT_RUNTIME.md)
actionable_next: After CF-11's gate fix, dispatch the Runtime audit against c2f0ba8e rather than a fresh team run; the ledger's handoff section specifies offline suite rerun, VERDICT recomputation from raw_rows.jsonl, prereg hash-chain check, REFUSE-list compliance, and the T2 fixture-bound caveat challenge.

Auditor must specifically adjudicate prereg-timing exposure: dev-phase test executions touched the same tasks before the 20:14:53Z freeze (log-only evidence in /tmp/spider_run_evidence/32887030457/logs.txt — keep that bundle until adjudicated).

If C1's negative survives audit, treat the NEXT_RUNTIME.md cycle-2 mission (near-repeat cell T3 + exploration-cost task family, predeclared VALID-NEGATIVE close rule) as the highest-information cheap dispatch for the lane.

findings.summary: Permission auto-rejection killed its SECOND confirmed lane session, this time aborting Product Beta PB-001's first build attempt (run 32799261473): at 05:54:29Z the beta_builder agent ran an environment-probing command touching ~/.config and /home/runner/.local/share/opencode/*, opencode emitted 'permission requested: external_directory (...); auto-rejecting' → 'Error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.' → whole session dead after ~3m40s of real work (architect snapshot verified; discovered working-tree graph/+shared/ are stripped-down variants vs pinned d41fe9b and vendored pinned sources to /tmp; playwright 1.62.0 + chromium-headless-shell installed; both target sites healthy). Workflow validator then failed 'Missing product_beta_build state'. Mechanism identical in class to Graph #5 (CF-2026-08-25-05) but a different permission object and different lane — this is now a systemic runtime defect, not a one-off. The builder branch b05d8f8 pushed anyway contains only re-committed architect content.
actionable_next: Apply CF-05's fix set product-wide AND verify by replay: pre-authorize known-safe parent paths (~/.config, ~/.local/share/opencode) read-only in lane opencode.json permission blocks, or make external_directory denials skip the single tool call instead of terminating the session.
Add the zero-diff guard: if a builder/architect session dies with no novel commits, do not push a misleadingly-named branch (b05d8f8 says 'build' but contains only architect content).
PB-001 can resume from the intact architect freeze 2c3bd28 + the logged vendoring plan; no architecture re-run is needed.

findings.summary: Un-retried opencode installer step is a whole-cycle kill switch: Product run 32820217763's BETA ARCHITECT job died ~4s after start when `curl --retry 3 --retry-all-errors -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` exited 1 with 'Failed to fetch version information' — the curl flags retry transport failures but the installer script's own version-metadata fetch has no retry wrapper at the step level (agent invocations get 6 attempts via run-opencode-with-retry.sh; install steps get none). Result: no v2 architecture, all downstream jobs skipped, empty cycle/product/32820217763/architect branch force-pushed. Every loop workflow shares this unguarded install pattern, so any installer hiccup can waste a scheduled dispatch per lane per occurrence.
durable_refs: git:origin/lab/product@1ecb1b8947b1111dd44ee6b2a85e4ff75b45b92b (the rev-2 authorization this run did deliver)
actionable_next: Wrap install steps with step-level retry (e.g. `for i in 1..5: curl ... && break` or reuse run-opencode-with-retry.sh semantics) in ALL loop workflows; verify opencode is already present as a fast-path skip (`command -v opencode`).
Treat 'installer failed' as retryable job failure rather than pushing an empty snapshot branch.

Consider persisting partial agent state (todo/prereg drafts) incrementally so externally-cancelled sessions leave resumable artifacts.

findings.summary: Unbrowse vendor-benchmark adversarial dossier exists and awaits reproduction (Intel cycle 2): scout recomputed the vendor's published CSV (ratio-of-means 3.58x, median 5.35x, 94/94 wins — headline partially survives its own data) while documenting CODE_VERIFIED harness defects (flat +2000 ms sleep in every Playwright baseline load; treatment-arm-only preference for server-reported timing over wall clock; inner_text('body') vs paper's stated CSS-selector methodology; single pass vs three; all rows marketplace-served/warmed), vendor honest negatives (~50% live retrieval coverage, Cloudflare/DataDome failures, claim-tier violations incl. 'peer-reviewed' preprint and '30x faster' marketing from the best domain), independent premise anchor (Song et al. ACL 2025 Findings: hybrid API+browsing >24% absolute over browsing-only WHEN APIs are pre-documented), new mechanism-family actors (Web Verbs arXiv:2602.17245, agent-browser derive-client, Kuri CDP broker, unbrowse-hermes), and a preregistration-ready A/B/C spec whose curl-level null isolates what the route abstraction adds beyond plain HTTP. All DURABLE on the scout branch but UNAUDITED; the first reproducer attempt was cancelled pre-prereg so nothing is contaminated.
actionable_next: Re-dispatch the Intel cycle-2 reproducer straight from the scout snapshot: freeze intel/prereg/cycle2_unbrowse_prereg.md first (conditions A/B/C, curl-level null, bias exclusions, per-site reporting that never pools no-API sites), then measure.

Reuse the scout's forensic checklist (raw-CSV recomputation, prose-vs-data diff, harness grep for sleeps/timing asymmetries/warmed rows, vendor-negative ledger) as the standing Intel template for any future vendor performance headline.

findings.summary: Audited-but-unintegrated snapshots cause duplicated stewardship spend: WP-006's evidence was carried forward bit-exact TWICE — first by run 32799587656 (carryforward + full independent audit PASS at 9acccb12 that no Director ever consumed because its attempt-2 rerun was cancelled), then again by run 32866107906 whose chain actually reached integration. Root cause: audited-but-unintegrated work leaves no machine-visible 'pending integration' trace for whoever dispatches the next physics run, so each new dispatch redoes legitimate-looking stewardship. Same class risk exists anywhere a Director job is skipped after a green audit (see CF-08's Graph retry storm). Positive note: verdict discipline held both times — neither stewardship run manufactured new confirmatory collection under the frozen stop rule.
actionable_next: Have lane workflows record a machine-readable pending-integration pointer (branch + gate path) into lane state whenever an audit reaches PASS but the Director does not run, and have dispatchers check it before authorizing fresh team/stewardship sessions.
Before any future WP-006-area dispatch: none is needed — TERMINATE_LANE stands, domain reopened under V3 via c15321c; treat further WP-006 stewardship as duplicate spend.

findings.summary: First distilled firing of the Product Supervisor's queued-run dedupe (run 32894986672, product-loop #9): a workflow_run trigger enqueued a redundant Product decision at 20:22:45Z while the PB-001 v4 lineage run 32886859788 was executing; #9 sat queued its entire 24m37s life (Jobs API total_count=0, zero artifacts, 0-byte raw log) on the single-slot spider-product-lane concurrency group and was cancelled at 20:47:22Z — exactly the situation product-supervisor.yml:53-62 cancels BY DESIGN ('Cancelling stale queued Product run ... while another Product run is in progress'). Precondition proven via sibling commits ddce3a3@20:31:13Z and 7657565@20:58:59Z bracketing the window. Positive: near-zero-cost dedupe prevented a duplicate director session racing lab/product. Negative: the specific cancelling supervisor instance is unattributable (its ::warning:: evidence lives only in supervisor logs, which hygiene prunes), and a local fetch failure can mimic the same fingerprint.
actionable_next: Treat 'conclusion=cancelled + 0 jobs + empty log' as a distinct benign signature in future distillation and pruning decisions — do not count it as a lane failure or retry it blindly.

Before pruning any such run, adjudicate against the live API (gh run view <id> --json jobs,conclusion) to rule out a fetch-harness artifact; this applies to 32894986672 itself (safe_to_prune=false until then).
Emit run-id-attributed receipts for supervisor cancellations (extend CF-02's receipt requirement to queue-state transitions) so dedupe events become self-documenting instead of forensic archaeology.

The Director explicitly directed the merge as the FIRST action at next activation; it has not happened yet.
actionable_next: Merge cycle/product/32886859788/builder@7657565 into lab/product BEFORE any further Product dispatch (single merge closes both the amendment and WP-8 gaps; verify kb_frozen.sqlite sha ...f89abd8f... and the four artifact_pins hashes after merge).
Until merged, treat lab/product PB-001 content as STALE relative to ddce3a3/7657565 and do not prune either cycle branch.

Adopt the structural rule: any state-referenced artifact must be reachable from a PUSHED ref before its producing session ends (extends CF-02 receipts to lane artifacts); named agent lineages should be pushed, not left local.

findings.summary: product-loop.yml's destructive wipe deletes COMMITTED-AT-HEAD authorization/build state on every dispatch and survived its own hotfix: `rm -f state/product_beta_request.json` (:63), `state/product_beta_architecture.json` (:136), `state/product_beta_build.json` (:236), `state/product_beta_audit.json` (:327) are still live at main HEAD, and both director sessions in run 32886859788 confirmed 'still live even at the hotfix commit 8f3980c'. Each dispatch burns agent time on detect-and-restore rituals and manufactures exactly the kind of mount-vs-durable divergence that produced CF-19.

Sweep sibling loop workflows for the same wipe pattern before their next dispatches.
Add a post-checkout assertion comparing wiped paths against git show HEAD:<path> so any future wipe is loud instead of silent.
